clue.text: Back away through burning framework

indicators.note: the reversed piece passes through the middle of the word for burning, so it is set inside

parts.note: scalding means burning hot

indicators.note: back says the word for away is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: away, as in 'off you go', means off

explanation.surface: Someone retreats through a fire on a building site's framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the word for away, and 'through' sets that run inside the word for burning. 'Back away' reads as one phrase meaning retreat, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaffolding is the temporary framework of poles and boards put up around a building.

clue.text: The whole — or not, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say means the word is only heard, so it can be spelt differently

parts.note: or not, the whole, is only part: some

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is complete or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or not' means not the whole, i.e. some, which is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the whole amount, the total.

clue.text: A national racing venue

parts.note: a Scot is a national of Scotland

explanation.surface: A national horse race track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'national' suggests the Grand National steeplechase; here it is a person of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Matisse, say, very interested at first in Goethe's work

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the title of Goethe's work

parts.note: Faust is Goethe's most famous play

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of very and interested

explanation.surface: Matisse is said to have been keen on Goethe's writings early on.
explanation.walkthrough: Matisse led the Fauves, the 'wild beasts' of early-1900s French painting, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Matisse led the Fauves, so he is an example of a Fauvist painter.

clue.text: Splashing around, figure lad might need one?

definitions.text: Splashing around, figure lad might need one?

indicators.note: splashing around tosses these letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy flailing in the water might need rescuing.
explanation.walkthrough: FIGURE LAD is rearranged; the whole clue also describes a boy in trouble in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeguard watches swimmers and rescues anyone struggling in the water.

clue.text: Charged, I note, though not capped

indicators.note: not capped says the word for note loses its first letter

parts.note: the tonic is the keynote of a musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone notes that, though accused, they were not picked for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the 'I' the page prints. I is followed by TONIC without its T; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic describes something composed of ions, which are electrically charged particles.

clue.text: Vessel where bun cooked in butter

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the word for butter

parts.note: a goat butts, so it is a butter

indicators.note: cooked says the letters of bun are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen container where a bun was cooked in butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the bun, and 'in' sets it inside the animal; 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunboat is a small armed warship, a naval vessel.

clue.text: Bully — one's mate!

definitions.meaning: to bully is to intimidate or browbeat someone
read 'Bully' as 'bull-y' and the bull's partner is the female of cattle

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'Bully' as the bull: 'one's mate' is the bull's female partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, and a cow is the female mate of a bull.

clue.text: Claws out with such a malicious nature?

definitions.text: Claws out with such a malicious nature?

parts.words: Claws out with such a malicious nature?
parts.note: a spiteful person said to have their claws out behaves like a feline

explanation.walkthrough: Spiteful remarks are called catty, as if the speaker had a cat's claws out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattiness is spitefulness, a malicious nature likened to a scratching cat.

clue.text: Transform maiden into brilliant fantasist

indicators.note: into says the first pieces go inside the word for brilliant

parts.note: witty means brilliantly clever
to alter is to transform
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl is turned into a dazzling dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming hero of a James Thurber story.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walter Mitty is a person who daydreams of heroic adventures, a fantasist, after Thurber's character.

clue.text: All currants going initially into cake played small but significant role

indicators.note: into says the picked letters go inside the word for cake

parts.note: a muffin is a small cake

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Currants in a cake have had a minor but vital part to play in the baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A, C, G from 'All currants going', and 'into' puts them inside MUFFIN after its M. 'played' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A MacGuffin is a plot device in film that drives the story while mattering little in itself, Hitchcock's term.

clue.text: Native Australian at a luncheon's tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in says the answer sits inside the run of words Australian at a luncheon's

explanation.surface: An Aboriginal Australian tucks into food at a lunch party.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'australiAN AT A Luncheon'; 'tucked in' signals the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, so a natal place is one's native land.

clue.text: Compiler's job situation

definitions.meaning: a crossword compiler's task is writing the puzzle
situation means a location or surroundings

explanation.definitionFit: Setting a crossword is the compiler's work, and a setting is the place where something is situated.

clue.text: Gyrating artiste, person on to peel off!

definitions.meaning: a performer who twirls and sways on stage
someone who comes on stage to take their clothes off

explanation.walkthrough: 'peel off' means undress, and 'on' means on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripteaser is a performer who undresses slowly to music, gyrating on stage.

clue.text: Sweet best to keep cold

indicators.note: to keep says the word for best holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: choice means the best, top-quality
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: The finest dessert should be kept chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate, sold from ice-cream vans.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc ice is a frozen confection, a sweet treat of ice cream coated in chocolate.

clue.text: Artist joining club in African city

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword shorthand for an artist
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A painter becomes a member of a sports club in an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco in North Africa.

clue.text: In foreign films, here's the Cotton Club under Calloway at last

indicators.note: under means, in a down clue, the word for club sits below the letter from Calloway

parts.note: a boll is the seed pod of the cotton plant

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of Calloway

parts.note: a wood is a golf club

explanation.surface: Cab Calloway, the bandleader, played the Cotton Club in old films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Cotton Club' suggests the Harlem jazz venue where Cab Calloway led his band; here it splits into cotton and club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollywood is the Hindi film industry of Mumbai, a source of foreign-language films.

clue.text: Current rate is offered with arm being twisted

indicators.note: being twisted says these letters are wrung out of shape into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The going rate is offered only when someone's arm is twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 0; the page reads 'with arm being twisted'. RATE IS plus ARM is rearranged; 'offered with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An air stream is a current of moving air.

clue.text: Centre of iron pot shortly supplied with very large, hot curry dish

indicators.note: centre of takes the two middle letters of iron
shortly says the word for pot loses its last letter

parts.note: ganja is slang for cannabis, or pot
OS stands for outsize, very large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A hot curry made in an iron pot with plenty of ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: RO from iron, GANJ (GANJA less A), OS and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogan josh is a spicy lamb curry of Kashmiri origin.

clue.text: Very cold in game, shivering at the end, maybe I do a lot of sniffing

definitions.text: maybe I do a lot of sniffing

indicators.note: in says the words for very cold go inside the word for game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
iced means very cold

indicators.note: at the end takes the final letter of shivering

explanation.surface: Someone frozen during a match, shivering at the end, confesses to sniffing a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person, as the dog itself would.
explanation.definitionFit: A police dog is trained to sniff out drugs or explosives, so it would say it does a lot of sniffing.

clue.text: Six-footer caught disease-succeeded escaping it at last

parts.note: C is the ... abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: escaping it at last says that letter leaves the end of the word for disease

parts.note: rickets is a bone disease
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tall man caught an illness and then recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' looks like a tall person but means an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is an insect, and insects have six legs, so it is a six-footer.

clue.text: Beneficial thing to remove lead from hound

indicators.note: to remove lead from says the word for hound loses its first letter

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hunting hound

explanation.surface: It is good to take the leash off a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing, something of benefit.

clue.text: A fool claiming error to be funny

indicators.note: claiming says the word for fool takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool
a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: An idiot thinks a mistake is hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fool' looks like one piece meaning an idiot, but the A stands alone in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing means entertaining, causing laughter.

clue.text: Delightful place making you smile, nothing less

indicators.note: making says the letters of you smile are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: O, shaped like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A lovely spot where you just cannot help smiling.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of YOU SMILE, less O ('nothing less'), are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium was the paradise of Greek myth, and the word now means any place of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Joint going to a bishop's head?

definitions.meaning: a woodworking joint where two pieces meet at an angle
what goes onto a bishop's head, his tall pointed hat

explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a corner joint in carpentry and also the tall headdress worn by a bishop.

clue.text: Sinful like love, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals that the made-up word is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so like love would be nought-y

explanation.surface: Asking whether love counts as sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring; 'nought-y' would mean like nought, and it is heard the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty means badly behaved, wicked in a mild or playful way.

clue.text: One supporting strike, inspiring a nation

indicators.note: supporting means, in a down clue, the letter for one sits below the rest
inspiring, breathing in, says the word for strike takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: to hit is to strike
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone backing a walkout motivates a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside HIT, and I comes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation sharing the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Farm animals as soup ingredient

definitions.meaning: livestock kept on a farm is a farmer's herd
a broth made by simmering bones, the base of a soup

explanation.definitionFit: Stock means livestock, and stock is also the liquid base made from bones for soups.

clue.text: Double G fitting old boy's seen, being adulterous

indicators.note: fitting says the words for old boy are fitted inside the double plus G

parts.note: a twin is a double
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A wedding guest in fine clothes, the son of the house, has been caught cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double G' reads as a pair of Gs, but 'Double' is the twin and G is just the letter; ''s seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing means deceiving a partner by secretly seeing someone else, being unfaithful.

clue.text: Date that could turn up?

indicators.note: turned up, read from the bottom in a down entry, these letters stay the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Asking whether a date will show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' suggests someone arriving for a date, but here it means reversing the entry, which reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a booked performance, a date on a band's tour.

clue.text: Free travel stopping short

indicators.note: stopping short says the word for travel loses its last letter

parts.note: to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Free travel comes to an abrupt halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid is to free or clear someone of something.

clue.text: Ashes, perhaps, held in this?

parts.note: Ashes looks like cremation remains or cricket, but means ash trees, which an environmentalist might embrace

explanation.surface: Wondering what an urn or a funeral holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ashes' suggests an urn or the cricket trophy; read it as ash trees, examples of trees, held in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree-hugging is the embracing of trees, a byword for passionate environmentalism.
